The re-carved path of arc 178 revisits vertices: 8797 five times in a row, and 10624, 10627, 9123, 1371 and 1257 twice each, with 10627 and 9123 reached twice at separated positions along the path (crossings 19-22 and again 30-32). The arc doubles back through the fan of vertex 8797 and around 10627, so it encloses a 3-face sliver [2682, 38513, 38515] bounded by nothing but itself, which no live patch owns. The contraction ran 2000+ collapses with loopDrags=109 (PATCH-111's new closing-loop routing) and 36 transits before the recarve; block at bias 0 in the same worktree loads end to end with loopDrags=163, so the loop routing is not wrong per se, but the self-revisiting path of arc 178 is where to start: whether it comes out of the contraction (a dragged tail routed through a vertex the arc's body already holds) or out of the recarve's taut step (dipRemoved / fanSlid) folding the path onto itself. The 25 trimmedEndCrossings in the recarve's snap line are also worth a look.

Reproduce in a worktree after PATCH-111 lands; the curvature bias must be set through PATCH-117's configuration path (NDirectionField curvature_bias port / QuadLayoutEngine.curvatureBias / the K key in QuadLayoutScene) once that lands, not by editing the field.

User direction 2026-09-19: bias -1 is the target for every mesh, so this is not an edge case behind a knob; block must load at -1.

UPDATE 2026-09-26: reproduces on master, independent of PATCH-111. Master's default curvature bias is now -1 (PATCH-117), and a plain `ixdar-cli model block` in quad-layout on master (44efbd15) fails with the identical message: the same 3 faces [2682, 38513, 38515], arc 178 from node 138 (vertex 18173) to node 16 (vertex 5526), the same chosen path. So no worktree, no hand edit of the bias and no other ticket is needed to reproduce it.

The same failure also comes out of PATCH-111's rewrite of the zero-arc collapse (every dragged arc fully released and re-routed by one Dijkstra, with routeDraggedTail, keepBody and the gate machinery removed), which is not landing. Two different collapse implementations producing the identical fold-back on the identical arc points away from the contraction's drag (unknown 1's first candidate; the routeDraggedTail named above only ever existed in PATCH-111's first attempt) and toward the recarve's taut step (pullStripsTaut: dipRemoved / fanSlid / endTrimmed) or the way arc 178 is first laid down. First step: record arc 178's path at the end of the contraction, before ArcNetworkRecarve runs, and check whether it already revisits vertices.

Timing: block at -1 runs just over 10 s on master (the contraction alone does 2000+ collapses and about 145000 edge splits), so give this one model a longer timeout (60 s) and keep every other model at 10 s.

Overlap: PATCH-119 (merge zero-arc clusters before the embedding) is in progress and changes which arcs are carved and dragged; if it lands first, re-run block and record whether the fold-back is still there before continuing.

UPDATE 2026-09-26: PATCH-111 (the plain-Dijkstra rewrite of the zero-arc collapse and ArcRerouter) has landed on master as 33cb78f7 after all; statements above that it is not landing are out of date. Numbers measured before it landed (the master sweep) are stale; re-baseline on current master.

2. The ticket records where arc 178's self-revisiting path came from (contraction drag, recarve taut step, or the initial route) and what the fix is; a re-carved arc path never visits a vertex twice, and requirePartition is not weakened.
3. block, botijo, rockerarm, fertility, elk, bolt and buddha at bias 0 keep the same '[contract]' and '[recarve]' counts and the same seamless metrics as master.

Dump arc 178's route before contraction, after each drag that touched it, and after the recarve taut step, to find where the revisit appears. 3. Fix; rerun block at -1 and the seven meshes at 0. 4. Launch entry with the bias property and a screenshot under tmp/.
unknowns: Is the fold-back produced by PATCH-111's keepBody loop routing (routeDraggedTail) when the moved end is routed through a vertex fan the arc's own body already passes, or by the recarve's fanSlid/dipRemoved taut step?
changes-made: Finding (patch-118, 2026-09-26): arc 178 is old arc 1260 (nodes 1859..16). Its contracted copy-vertex path at the end of NetworkContraction.contract is simple (no arc's contracted path revisits a vertex on block at -1). Refined onto the clean copy the route is an out-and-back hairpin: the outward leg crosses the fans of 9123 and 10627 near their rims, wraps 8797 once, and the return leg runs back through the same source faces and exactly through vertices 10627 (crossing 30) and 9123 (crossing 32). The taut pass only removed one dip around 8786 and a fan slide; strip 178 before and after it has the same hairpin, so the taut step does not create the revisit. The revisit is created by SnappingCarve's corner assignment: grantCorners gives the outward crossings on 6003..10627 / 8807..10627 (and 8815..9123 / 6003..9123) their shared corner 10627 (9123), which the same arc already claimed for its later through-vertex crossing; releaseRepeatedCorners only releases the later run of a repeated corner and never a through-vertex crossing, so here it releases nothing and the path pinches 10627 -> lanes -> 8797 -> 1371 -> 10627, enclosing [2682, 38513, 38515].

Finding 2: the hairpin is laid in one drag. Watching old arc 1260 through the contraction: its path goes from 26 vertices / 23 source faces / 0 source-face revisits to 292 vertices / 56 source faces / 7 revisits at step 1171, the collapse of arc 2141, whose drag re-routes it from node 1287 onto node 1859 (ZeroArcCollapseOperator.dragArcEndOntoVertex -> routeDraggedTail, a full ArcRerouter route that prefers any unsplit detour over a split). Nothing after that step removes the detour. Making the carve's corner release keep the through-vertex run (so the path stays simple) gets block past requirePartition but then fails in GridMapOptimizer ('starting grid map has 45 folded triangles', patch 149, signedArea 0): the U between the two legs of arc 178 lies in patch 149 and touches only arc 178, so its triangles map onto that one straight side. So the hairpin itself has to go, not just the revisit.

Fix in progress (patch-118 worktree, uncommitted): ArcNetworkRecarve replays the arcs, and any arc whose taut strip still passes one constraint face twice (a fold) is re-routed on the contracted mesh by a shortest-length Dijkstra restricted to the faces of its two flanking patches (flooded from the arc's own edges, walled by every other arc) and never touching another arc or node, then the replay is redone. The flanks form one disk, so the new route is homotopic and the patch combinatorics do not change. New requireSimplePaths check after the carve throws when a laid arc path visits a vertex twice (requirePartition untouched). SnappingCarve.releaseRepeatedCorners now keeps the run that passes exactly through the vertex and releases the other run's edge crossings (it used to release only a later run, never a through-vertex one). On block at -1 only arc 178 (old 1260) folds; it goes from 392 to 28 contracted vertices; recarve passes (nodes=154 arcs=316 patches=158), the grid map starts unfolded and relaxes (flipped=0). Block then fails later, in ExtractedPatchGrids.completeNode: 'ring walk at node 10 expects port 5379 for arc end 223 but it holds 5380'. Node 10 is a valence-5 critical node 16.5 units from arc 178, not on patches 86/149; four of its five arcs (22, 150, 151, 111, all quantized 1) leave it within ~40 degrees of each other in the recarved mesh (22/150/151 start on three lanes of one edge), so after relaxation all five quad ports at node 10 fall in patch 103's triangles and two arc ends match port 5380. That is a separate layout-quality problem at node 10 (contraction geometry), not the fold-back. Sweep vs master: every other model's [recarve], [contract] and [seamless] Metrics lines are identical (no other model has a folded arc); botijo timed out at 10 s under load (master 8.8 s) with identical recarve counts.

After PATCH-111 landed (master 9f5a5fce): plain master still fails block at -1 the same way, arc 178 from node 138 (vertex 18173) to node 16 (vertex 5526), same chosen corners through 8797/10627/9123; the region's face ids moved to [2682, 38518, 38520] because the lane count differs. patch-118 synced onto 9f5a5fce cleanly. With the fix on the synced tree: block recarve passes (nodes=154 arcs=316 patches=158, taut dipRemoved=26 fanSlid=99), grid-optimize relaxes with flipped=0/44918, then the same ExtractedPatchGrids failure at node 10 ('expects port 5359 for arc end 223 but it holds 5360'). New baseline sweep of landed master (tmp/sweep-master2) vs the fix (tmp/sweep-fix2): every [recarve], [contract], [seamless] Metrics and [grid-optimize] line of bolt, hand, botijo, elk, fertility, both rockerarms and buddha is identical; feline and buddha time out at 10 s in both, fandisk fails in both with the pre-existing 'arc 815 runs exactly through copy vertex 684'. The only differences are block's new recarve and grid-optimize lines.

DoD 2 record: arc 178's self-revisit comes from neither the drag nor the taut step alone. The drag (collapse of arc 2141, step 1171) laid old arc 1260 as a simple but folded hairpin on the contracted mesh (legs one lane apart, the tip wrapped round 8797); the recarve's taut pass cannot zip it because the tip circles a vertex; then the carve's corner assignment gave the outward leg corners 10627 and 9123 (the corners its crossings share with their next edge) that the return leg passes exactly through, and releaseRepeatedCorners only ever released a later edge run, so the laid path visited 10627 and 9123 twice. Fix: ArcNetworkRecarve re-routes any arc whose taut strip passes one face twice by a shortest route inside its two flanking patches on the contracted mesh and replays; requireSimplePaths now refuses any laid path that revisits a vertex; SnappingCarve keeps a corner for the run that passes exactly through it. Tests: CarveFoldBackCornerTest (two vertex fans; master's release rule lays [5, 0, 2, 3, 1, 0, 6], the fix a simple path) and RecarveFoldedArcTest (a 7x5 grid, two patches, middle arc folded round W and back through C on a split copy; master throws 're-carved arc 6 visits copy vertex 17 twice', release alone keeps the U [5, 6, 11, 36, ...], the fix re-carves it straight down its column [5, 6, 7, 8, 9]). mvn test: 320 run, 0 failures. DoD 1 is not met: that failure needs its own ticket (or PATCH-119's zero-arc merge may change node 10).

Finding (node 10, 2026-09-26): an extraction bug, not upstream geometry. Node 10 (critical, valence 5, arcs in ring order 22|61|150|95|111|103|23|119|151|81) is fine in the relaxed grid map (flipped=0, fan angles sum to 450 degrees), but relaxation squeezes the thin 3D wedges (patches 119/81/61/95 open 22.6/7.8/18/24.3 degrees) and patch 103's corner wraps 377 degrees round the node, so all five ports lie in patch-103 faces and two of them (5358 at 90, 5359 at 450) carry the same direction turns=1 in 103's chart. ExtractedPatchGrids.anchorNodes direct-matched arc 23 (dir (0,10) in 103) to the first, 5358; chainArrivalConsistent could not reject it because arc 23's far node 72 is free. Arc 111's match 5360 is verified (only 5360 reaches critical node 29), and the ring walk from it (111=5360, 23=5359, 151=5358, 22=5357, 150=5356) agrees with arc 150's own check (only 5356 reaches critical node 15). Fix: the direct match takes a (patch, direction) port only when exactly one chain-consistent port carries it; an ambiguous pair names neither and the ring walk fills the end from a verified anchor. Block at -1 now loads: [patch-grids] patches=158 directMatches=181 rejected=0 ringCompleted=345 refitNodes=106, '[quad-layout] patch surfaces' reached.

Test for the node-10 mechanism: WrappedCornerPortMatchTest (unit.mesh), a hand-authored closed layout (two valence-5 poles, ten valence-3 corners, five free valence-4 spoke ends; 22 nodes, 40 arcs, 20 one-quad patches) that is its own quad mesh. The top pole's five ports all lie in the first cap patch with directions t, t+1, .., t+4, so spokes 0 and 4 share one direction, and the port list starts at spoke 4. With the first-found rule the regrouping throws 'ring walk at node 0 expects port 4 for arc end 6 but it holds 3' (block's failure); with the fix only spoke 1 is matched directly, the ring walk completes the pole and every quad lands in its patch.

Verified 2026-09-26: block at -1 alone under 60 s loads in 7.3 s, '[quad-layout] patch surfaces' reached, [patch-grids] patches=158 directMatches=181 rejected=0 ringCompleted=345 refitNodes=106; tmp/patch-118-block-bias-1.png shows the full layout. Sweep tmp/sweep-fix4 vs tmp/sweep-master2 (timings and the JVM-cumulative exactSigns stripped): every [recarve], [contract], [seamless] Metrics and [grid-optimize] line of bolt, hand, botijo, elk, fertility and both rockerarms is identical, feline's and buddha's partial lines agree as far as they run (both time out at 10 s on master too), fandisk fails in both with 'arc 815 runs exactly through copy vertex 684'; block's only differences are its new recarve and grid-optimize lines and that it now loads. The ExtractedPatchGrids change runs after grid-optimize, so it cannot move any watched line. mvn test: 321 run, 0 failures. ixd wt done passed and marked REVIEW.
